name: Koplin 3 Canonical Surface Atlas
description: Canonical authored materialisation of selected 1 km × 1 km surface tiles on Koplin 3, beginning at the centre of Concordia and expanding outward in a clockwise square spiral. It is a visual atlas layer, distinct from the reusable Mobile landscape tileset and from mutable per-save game maps.

phaseOne.purpose: Establish the capital core, inner city, outer metropolitan belt and first peri-urban/rural transitions before the public atlas browser is added.

capitalPlacement.environment: cool-to-warm temperate, well-watered metropolitan plain within the Zoran continent's historic fault-and-ore belt
capitalPlacement.planningRationale: The capital deliberately sits in a region associated with Zoran technical institutions while functioning as a Commonwealth city for all three peoples. Its location supports rapid continental transport, abundant landscaped water and expansion from dense civic core into green suburbs and productive countryside.

macroWorldPlan.role: hot equatorial and tropical biomass-rich continent
macroWorldPlan.visualDirection: lush coasts, rivers, wetlands, dense agriculture, forest belts, tropical cities and large ecological preserves

macroWorldPlan.role: temperate, faulted and ore-rich continent; location of Concordia
macroWorldPlan.visualDirection: temperate forests and grasslands, mineral highlands, mature cities, old technical centres, farms, rail corridors and managed watersheds

macroWorldPlan.role: cold polar and sub-polar continent with deep energy and mineral resources
macroWorldPlan.visualDirection: tundra, snow, exposed rock, long-winter settlements, heavy infrastructure, protected heated agriculture and dramatic extraction landscapes

macroWorldPlan.role: island chains, shelves and polar archipelagos outside the three major continental masses
macroWorldPlan.visualDirection: remote ports, research stations, fisheries, volcanic or glacial islands, nature reserves and sparse settlement

styleLock.reference: User-approved MineIT building-art language adapted to a 1 km city/terrain atlas
styleLock.camera: high oblique isometric/axonometric aerial, consistent orientation on every tile
styleLock.lighting: bright temperate local midday with consistent sun direction and crisp shadows
styleLock.architecture: polished advanced Commonwealth design: white and light-grey composite structures with strong orange accents, dark mechanical details, blue glass, exposed but clean infrastructure, glass biodomes and integrated planting
styleLock.rendering: ultra-detailed AAA city-builder / colony-builder environment art; full bleed edge-to-edge; readable at overview scale
styleLock.mood: prosperous, mature, highly networked and materially comfortable; never dystopian, ruined or cyberpunk-grimy
styleLock.textRule: No readable labels, logos, UI or watermarks in the artwork
styleLock.terrainRule: As density falls, retain the same visual language in roads, utilities, farms, villages and terrain infrastructure rather than forcing city architecture into wilderness.

adjacencyRules.promptEdges: Every tile stores north/east/south/west boundary anchors. Shared boundaries are derived deterministically so both neighboring prompts describe the same crossing features.
adjacencyRules.imageReferences: When generating a tile, use already-generated orthogonal neighbours listed in referenceTileIds as image references wherever tooling allows. Prefer the direct predecessor and any west/south/north/east neighbour already present.
adjacencyRules.seamReview: Reject or regenerate obvious broken roads, rail lines, waterways, lighting changes or scale changes before an image is accepted as canonical.
adjacencyRules.densityGradient: Rings 0-1 are civic core; 2 inner city; 3 middle city; 4 outer metropolitan belt; 5 begins peri-urban, greenbelt, farms, woodland, villages and other lower-density land.

websitePlan.implementationTrigger: after a useful first atlas area is generated, targeted initially at the first 100 tiles
websitePlan.viewer: pan-and-zoom coordinate grid using worldAtlasTiles records and canonical image keys
websitePlan.tilePanel: show coordinate, sequence, batch, ring, district, description and generation metadata
websitePlan.navigation: render by coordinate, not generation order, while optionally visualising spiral order and generation batches
